guidance: The result is a cut size, not a finished garment size: seam and hem allowances and any pattern repeat still have to be added. Measure the shrinkage on a swatch of the same fabric washed the same way, and check the warp and weft directions separately, because they usually differ.
method: Fabric shrinks by a percentage of its original length, so the cut size is the finished size divided by one minus the shrinkage fraction. Length shrinkage and width shrinkage are separate percentages, measured along the selvedge and across it. In percentage mode they are entered directly, from 0 to 25 percent. In wash-test mode four swatch measurements give them: shrink percent = (before - after) / before x 100, read separately for length and width; a washed sample that measures the same or longer is refused because it implies growth, which this allowance does not cover. The cut length and cut width are finished / (1 - shrink/100), and the extra to allow is the difference in each direction. An optional length on hand is run forward through the same length shrink and compared with the finished length, reporting the finished length that piece will yield, whether it is long enough, and the shortfall. Shrinkage of 8 percent or more in either direction is flagged as heavy. Finished sizes are limited to 1 to 10000 in the chosen unit, shrinkage to 0 to 25 percent, swatch measurements to 1 to 1000 before washing and 0.1 to 1000 after, and fabric on hand to 0.1 to 100000. Width, seam and hem allowances, pattern repeats and directional nap are not modelled, and the length on hand is checked against the cut length only. The calculation runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
